headline: AI SDLC.
From task to review.
description: Orchestrate your software development lifecycle with AI. xDev Hive connects your team, coding agents, and repositories: claim tasks, prepare context, track runs, review results, and preserve lessons for the next task.
map_label: Team and agent orchestration across AI SDLC
map_caption: Tasks drive the work. Context guides agents. Results are reviewed, and lessons feed the next development cycle.

features.title: Shared documents
features.text: Manage standards, project instructions, and technical decisions with versions, history, and diffs. Sync documents to AGENTS.md in your repository.

features.title: Memory across sessions
features.text: Save decisions and lessons for the next agent to find. Search within a project or across shared team memory, with support for accented and unaccented Vietnamese.

features.title: Skills for the team
features.text: Keep working procedures in one place, with shared and project-specific skills. Claude Code loads them from the repository; other agents read them through MCP.

features.title: Tasks and runs
features.text: Track tasks, agent claims, and results within a project. The desktop app runs coding agents on your machine and reports their status to the hub.

features.title: Human review
features.text: Agents propose document and skill changes; administrators review the diff before approval. New hub memory is also reviewed before other agents can use it.

features.title: Web hub and desktop
features.text: Use the desktop app with local data or connect to a shared hub. Manage accounts, access permissions, and agent tokens on the hub.

workflow_description: Start with a repository and a clear task. Connect agents to project standards, track the work, and feed reviewed lessons back into project context.

steps.title: Prepare tasks and context
steps.text: Connect a repository, define the work, and give agents relevant standards, skills, and memory.

steps.title: Run agents and track results
steps.text: Agents claim tasks; the desktop runner executes work in your configured environment. Your team tracks status, logs, and repository-linked results.

steps.title: Review and feed lessons back
steps.text: Inspect code results through PRs or MRs and review proposed knowledge updates. Approved decisions, skills, and memory guide the next task.

start_title: Start AI SDLC with your repository.
start_description: Find the source, installation requirements, and instructions for running the hub or desktop app in the project README.
hero_note: AI SDLC — the software development lifecycle with AI, with your team making the decisions.
story_label: From AI coding to AI SDLC
story_title: Finish a task. Move the development cycle forward.
story_intro: Writing code is one part of the work. Teams also need to assign tasks, give agents the right context, track results, and review what comes next. Hive connects those steps with project knowledge, so multiple agents work within a process with clear responsibility.
problems: Tasks need clear ownership, status, and dependencies so teams can track work in progress and results awaiting review.
Agents need relevant standards, skills, and technical decisions before starting. Teams need to inspect that context.
After reviewing a task, preserve, approve, and retrieve decisions and gotchas so the next task builds on what the team learned.
showcase_intro: The real Hive interface running on a separate demo hub. Atlas and the content shown are illustrative data.

panels.label: Tasks
panels.title: A task, an owner, a result.
panels.text: Create tasks, declare dependencies, and track progress from todo to completion. Time-limited claims help coordinate work across agents.

panels.label: Context
panels.title: Know what your agents will receive.
panels.text: Inspect context documents and distinguish team standards from project instructions before distributing them to repositories.

panels.label: Skills
panels.title: Turn good practice into shared procedures.
panels.text: Manage team skills and project-specific overrides. Claude Code loads synced repository skills; other agents discover and read them through MCP.

panels.label: Proposals
panels.title: Agents propose. Your team decides.
panels.text: Inspect the reason and diff before approving document or skill changes. A proposal based on an older document version is flagged as a conflict.

panels.label: Memory
panels.title: Start with what the team already knows.
panels.text: Keep decisions, conventions, and gotchas. Agents search project memory; administrators approve entries, revisit old knowledge, and review it when referenced files change.

panels.label: Documents
panels.title: Standards the whole team can read.
panels.text: Organize documents by team and project. Read, edit, version, and inspect changes; sync relevant instructions to repositories so agents can find them when needed.

Put conventions into shared documents, review agent proposals, and preserve technical decisions with their rationale.

boundary_title: Administrators remain part of the decision.
boundary_text: Hive uses permissions and review to govern shared documents, skills, and memory. Coding agents run through the CLI, account, and environment you configure. Quotas, sandboxing, and repository integrations depend on those systems.
setup_title: Start on your machine. Grow with your team.
setup_options: Use the desktop app, add a repository, and configure your coding agents. Keep your data and runs on your own machine.
Run the web hub, set up accounts and permissions, and connect desktop machines and agents through MCP. Follow the README for Docker setup.
faq: Does Hive replace a coding agent?
Hive provides knowledge and coordination. Coding work is still performed by agents such as Claude Code, Codex, or Gemini CLI.
Do all runs require a new API key?
The runner uses the CLIs and profiles you configure. Subscription or API usage, quotas, and costs depend on each agent provider.
Can I use it without a shared hub?
Yes. The desktop app supports local data. A hub adds shared accounts, documents, memory, and coordination across machines.
Can agents rewrite shared standards on their own?
In the Hive workflow, agents submit proposals. A permitted reviewer inspects the diff and approves it; stale proposals are flagged as conflicts.
Are the images and film a live system demo?
The screenshots show the real Hive frontend on a temporary hub with Atlas demo data. The film is an illustrated product overview with synthetic narration, not an agent or integration benchmark.
